item.title: A machine-learning method for the estimation of the background from jets misidentified as hadronic tau lepton decays (CMS TAU-25-001)
item.dc:creator: CMS Collaboration
item.description:
How central to this topic: peripheral. This is a background-estimation method for jet→τh fakes. Jet structure enters only through simple proxies, not substructure observables.

What they did. MUFFIN replaces binned fake factors N_pass/N_fail with a continuous transfer factor, the ratio of calibrated XGBoost class probabilities. - The nominal model is a four-class BDT (data pass/fail, genuine-τ simulation pass/fail). Genuine-τ contamination is subtracted inside the weight: w = (P_pass^data − P_pass^τsim)/(P_fail^data − P_fail^τsim). - No simulation of the targeted fake process is used for the data-derived QCD and W+jets factors. - Inputs, in order of feature importance: τh decay mode, then p_T(jet)/p_T(τh), then p_T(τh), N_jets, N_b, η, φ, and a data-period label. The p_T(jet)/p_T(τh) ratio is the one substructure-like handle, capturing how much of the seed jet’s momentum the HPS candidate captures. - Temperature scaling gives T* ≈ 0.99–1.00, so the BDT outputs are essentially already calibrated. - Statistical uncertainty comes from a 50-model bootstrap ensemble.

Results. Data are 62.4 fb⁻¹ at 13.6 TeV. In validation-region closure, MUFFIN gives a lower mean |Poisson pull| than fake factors in τhτh and τμτh. The gains are largest in η and decay mode (which fake factors marginalise over) and at high p_T. The abstract quotes up to 70% lower jet→τh systematic uncertainty. Total jet→τh yield uncertainty is 6% (τhτh) and 5% (τμτh). The analysis-dependent extrapolation term (≲10%) dominates; the flat non-closure term is 5%.

Caveats. - W+jets and tt̄ are validated only in simulation, since there is no clean data validation region. - A residual ΔR non-closure in τμτh resembles the fake-factor behaviour, pointing to a missing input variable. - Pull values appear only in the figures. - The provided text truncates during the signal-region application section.

item.title: Precision Tokenization for Multi-Modal Data in High Energy Physics
item.dc:creator: Jeffrey Krupa et al.
item.description:
What they did. Residual-VQ-VAE tokenizers with Transformer encoders and decoders, scanned over codebook size K, code dimension d and number of residual stages Q. Modalities are ATLAS JetSet tracks (20 features) and COCOA tracks, topoclusters, and calorimeter cells (8×8 patches with occupancy and energy loss). Fidelity is set against information fraction I = Q·log₂K/(32D).

Headline numbers. Reaching the 1% jet p_T IQR/median target: | Modality | Configuration | Compression | Resolution | |—|—|—|—| | JetSet | (32768, 8, 4) | 10.7× | 0.82% | | COCOA tracks | (4096, 8, 3) | 4.4× | 0.68% | | COCOA topoclusters | (4096, 8, 6) | 3.6× | 0.39% | | COCOA cells (best, misses target) | not stated | 11× | 1.24% |

  • Learned tokenizers need up to 2.4× fewer bits than per-feature binning.
  • The in-context (Transformer) encoder beats an MLP: 0.82% vs 1.27%.

Design rules. Use multiple residual stages (single-stage collapses), use large K, scale d with the bit budget and the target’s intrinsic dimension, and bin (η,φ) outside the quantizer when coordinates dominate the feature set.

Downstream tasks. - Particle flow: with positions binned outside the quantizer, IQR/median is 0.086 vs 0.0845 for continuous inputs (about 2% relative). - b-tagging: at 60 bits per constituent, tokens retain 73–93% of continuous-input rejection. At ε_b = 0.7, light-jet rejection is 1170 vs 1370 and τ-jet rejection 354 vs 451. - Degradation at 30 bits: charm rejection drops to 19.1 vs 42.0, so high-rejection tails are where tokenization costs most.

Caveats. - The resolution metric measures tokenizer error only, comparing reconstructed constituents with themselves before tokenization. - COCOA tracks are smeared, not reconstructed. - Table 4’s COCOA-track value of 0.068% looks inconsistent with Table 1’s 0.68% (a unit slip is likely). - No substructure observables (e.g. mass, N-subjettiness) are checked explicitly.

Link between the two papers. Both swap hand-binned representations of jet-constituent information for learned ones. The tokenization paper quantifies what that costs; MUFFIN shows what it gains for a data-driven background estimate.

item.title: The hidden sunrise in the energy-energy correlator
item.dc:creator: Matthew D. Schwartz et al.
item.description:
This paper completes the analytic NNLO EEC in 𝒩=4 SYM. Ref. [1] had left one unevaluated two-fold integral F_R(ζ); this work evaluates it.

Polylogarithmic pieces. - Partial fractioning in the inner variable splits F_R into three parts: F_red₁ (purely polylogarithmic), F_K₁, and F_R₂. - F_R₂ has to be kept as a whole, because red₂ and K₂ separately diverge like (1−z̄)⁻² log²(1−z̄). - The polylog remainder P(ζ) = F_red₁ + Δ consists of HPLs of weight ≤5 on the alphabet {ζ, 1−ζ}. Notably, the √ζ letter present at NLO is absent, and the weight is non-uniform.

Elliptic sector. - The two square-root discriminants Q₁ and Q₂ are related by the Möbius map w = z̄/(z̄−1). Both are isomorphic to the equal-mass sunrise curve under S = (ζ−1)/ζ, and the j-invariants match identically. - Under this map the physical region 0<ζ<1 lands in the Euclidean sunrise region. The odd-looking singular point ζ = −1/8 is the 9m² threshold. - The coupled system for F_K₁, F_R₂ and a companion integral S₀ involves 𝓛 = ζ∘L_PF∘ζ⁻¹, which is second order. This bounds the result at elliptic: no K3 or Calabi–Yau geometry can appear. - Subtracting the coupled equations shows Δ = F_R₂ − F_K₁ is polylogarithmic, giving F_R = 2F_K₁ + P. - S₀ is written as weight-5 iterated Eisenstein integrals for Γ₁(6). The letters are ω₀ and ω₁ plus two new modular-weight-3 letters, ψ₁ω₀ and ζψ₁ω₀.

Numerics and the collinear limit. - Evaluation is by truncated q-series, with the collinear limit ζ→0 at q→0. About 75 terms give 50 digits at ζ = 3/11 (q₀ ≈ 0.17). - Per their error estimate N_dig ≈ N log₁₀(1/q₀) − 3, convergence degrades toward back-to-back, where q→1.

How central this is to the topic. The relevance to jet substructure is indirect: this is a full-angle, fixed-order result in 𝒩=4. The value for jets is mainly a clean collinear-limit expansion and a template for the QCD elliptic sector, which the authors assert but do not compute.

Caveats. - The provided text is truncated before the bootstrap section, so I can’t assess those results. - Much of the technical work was done with AI under human supervision.

item.title: A compact, interrogable Tree Tensor Network Jet Tagger on Lund declustering trees
item.dc:creator: Fabrizio Napolitano et al.
item.description:
Architecture. A single shared trilinear core C ∈ ℝ^{6×χ×χ×χ} is contracted recursively along the C/A declustering tree. Inputs are the five LundNet5 coordinates in a projective-sphere encoding, plus a shared MLP residual. Optional QCD gates (α_s and splitting functions) and Sudakov gates modulate the tree message. At χ = 8 the model has 4014 parameters, against about 391k for LundNet5 and 366k for ParticleNet. Samples are particle-level Pythia (training) and Herwig (transfer), 2M jets per generator.

Performance:

Task Evaluation TTN LundNet5 ParticleNet
q/g native AUC 0.8917 0.8941 0.9014
q/g Pythia→Herwig AUC 0.8114 0.8098 0.8107
top native AUC 0.9531 0.9574 0.9592
top native 1/ε_B at ε_S = 0.5 132 187 204
top Pythia→Herwig AUC 0.9472 0.9474 0.9479
  • Transfer AUCs agree within 0.002 across all three taggers in both tasks.
  • The physics gates change AUC by at most 0.0011, so they bring no measurable gain.

Bond-dimension and k_t-cut scans. - q/g is nearly flat in χ, while top tagging improves with χ. - The default configuration has no k_t cut and is therefore not IRC safe. Imposing ln(k_t/GeV) > −2 restores IRC safety at a cost of ≤0.003 AUC. - Raising the cut to 1 narrows the Pythia→Herwig gap; in top tagging the transfer AUC even exceeds the native one.

What’s new: interrogability. Because the same map acts at every node, a tree truncated at depth D is processed with the learned vacuum state, exactly as at leaves during training. - Pythia/Herwig latent divergence concentrates at depths 10–15 and at ln k_t < 0, mostly in gluons. - In the primary plane the divergence sits at ln(1/Δ) > 4.

Caveats. - All results use a single training seed. - Baselines are not parameter-matched. - The smaller relative transfer loss partly reflects the TTN’s lower nominal performance. - The readout was never trained on truncated trees. - There is no detector simulation.

Connection to the other paper. There is no substantive link to the EEC paper.

item.title: The Back-to-Back Plateau of the Energy-Energy Correlator from Weak to Strong Coupling
item.dc:creator: Hao Chen et al.
item.description:
Relevance. This is only loosely a substructure paper. It studies the back-to-back (Sudakov) endpoint of the full-event EEC in 𝒩=4 SYM, not the collinear region inside jets. QCD jet measurements appear only as motivation. The overlap with the topic is energy-correlator technology.

What they did. Chen, Moult, Wang and Zhu resum both leading-power (LP, y⁻¹) and next-to-leading-power (NLP, y⁰) back-to-back logarithms through N³LL, including 1/N_c² terms. The method is the large-spin and twist-conformal-block pipeline of Chen–Zhou–Zhu, in five steps: - twist-2 anomalous dimensions γ₁…γ₄ and OPE-coefficient corrections r₁…r₃ are put into a finite-difference large-spin basis; - these are lifted to the twist-conformal-block basis; - crossing of Φ(u,v) is used, which avoids needing twist-4 data; - a Mellin/light transform is applied; - the coefficients are matched to fixed-order data.

Results. - NLP towers and checks. They give closed forms for the generic NLP coefficients C_k^NLP(n). Only C₂^NLP(1) and C₄^NLP(2) need fixed-order input; the remaining expansion terms agree with the known fixed-order expansion through three loops. - Structure of the NLP function. The resummed NLP function G contains an erf(√a L_y/√2) tower. This term survives as y→0, giving a finite NLP shift to the plateau beyond the essential-singular LP term P_LP ~ a^{-1/2}e^{1/(2a)}. - Interpolation. A two-parameter interpolation (p=2.34, q=1.81) is built to match the weak-coupling LP asymptotics and the strong-coupling result 1+1/a. It is fit to planar bootstrap points.

Caveats. - The residual endpoint term H₀(a) is still undetermined beyond these logarithms. - The perturbative description visibly degrades by a ~ 1/4, and the string expansion only reaches down to a ~ 0.5. The window in between is covered only by the fit. - The interpolation is phenomenological, by the authors’ own description. - Transfer to QCD (running coupling, hadronization) is posed as an open question, not addressed.

Agentic workflow. The calculation used a human-in-the-loop setup with GPT-5.5. Humans had to fix the truncation depth (Step 5), working backward from the final observable. In an independent test of seven models on 15 steps, the best scored 10/15. No model solved the large-spin expansion, the explicit twist-block sum, or the three-loop check. The aggregate pass counts in the text are unfilled placeholders (“x out of 28”).

item.title: Boosted top tagging via lepton-in-jet topology for vector-like quark searches in FCC-hh
item.dc:creator: Sanchari Bhattacharyya et al.
item.description:
This paper builds a lepton-seeded tagger for boosted t→bℓν at √s=100 TeV. Everything is defined in a ΔR<0.4 cone around a non-isolated lepton with p_T>100 GeV. The study uses PYTHIA plus Delphes with the FCC-hh card. The tagger is a four-class classifier (t_lep, t_had, b, c) trained separately in seven lepton-p_T bins from 0.1 TeV to above 3 TeV.

The two taggers take different inputs: - DNN: engineered observables, including displaced-track ΔR and multiplicity, Q_κ jet charge, tower isolation, jet mass, and τ_N ratios. - ParT: nine features per constituent (tracks, towers and the lepton) and pairwise angular attention biases.

Main results - Leptonic-top AUC: ParT gives 0.994–0.997, flat in p_T. The DNN rises from 0.981 to 0.996. - Efficiency at score >0.4: ParT reaches 94% to 97%, the DNN 89% to 96%. - High-p_T crossover: above ~2 TeV the DNN has lower mistag rates for all three background classes. The authors read this as constituent information helping only while the decay products stay angularly resolved. - Track-only inputs (1.0–1.5 TeV bin): ParT 0.981, GNN 0.964, DNN 0.942. The DNN drops from 0.992 with full inputs, so the high-level approach relies heavily on calorimeter information, which is the part most exposed to pile-up. - Cone size: shrinking the cone to 0.2 leaves performance essentially unchanged. - Event level: feeding the tagger into a B′→tW search gives 5σ discovery reach of ~7 TeV for Γ/m<25%, or ~10 TeV for Γ/m≲50%, at 30 ab⁻¹.

Caveats - There is no pile-up overlay. The only proxy is raising the track threshold from 5 to 20 GeV, which leaves AUCs unchanged. - Light-flavour jets are excluded from tagger training. - Diboson events with boosted Z or W→cs produce a peak near tagger score 1. - The event classifier is trained only at 5 TeV. - The ParT+DeepSVDD anomaly result (AUC 0.894) treats the leptonic top itself as the nominal class, so its relevance to anomaly searches is limited.

item.title: Three-loop rapidity anomalous dimension for jet-veto cross sections
item.dc:creator: Samuel Abreu et al.
item.description:
This paper supplies the last missing ingredient for N³LL resummation of the colour-singlet p_T^jet<p_T^veto cross section. The authors compute γ_ν⁽³⁾⁽R²⁾ from the three-loop SCET soft function, using the exponential rapidity regulator, for anti-k_t, C/A and k_t. The two-loop beam and soft functions, four-loop cusp and three-loop non-cusp anomalous dimensions were already known.

Method. The key device is a non-physical “Reference Simplified Variable” (RSV). It applies the veto to the total p_t of each correlated cluster in the non-abelian-exponentiation decomposition, so it is R-independent and factorises cluster by cluster.

  • ln𝒮_RSV is a Bessel-kernel transform of the TMD soft function. This gives γ_ν,RSV=γ_ν,⊥+(α_s/4π)³ 323C_R b_0²ζ_3 at three loops.
  • The remainder Δ𝒮 vanishes for single emission, so the two-loop single-real amplitude is never needed. Its singularity structure also drops by two orders: at three loops it has only one-loop-type poles.
  • The remainder splits into III, CCI and CCC pieces, which scale at small R as R⁴, R²lnR² and ln²R² respectively. Integrations are done semi-numerically with Cuba, cross-checked with VegasFlow.

Results. Three loops is the first order at which the result depends on the clustering algorithm, but the spread between the three algorithms is very mild. For n_f=5, C_R=C_A, the three-loop coefficients are:

R Three-loop coefficient Two-loop coefficient (for comparison)
0.1 77165 ± 0.36‰ 2174.69
0.4 28537 ± 0.38‰ 1135.60
0.8 6645 ± 0.97‰ 498.59

At p_T^veto=30 GeV the three-loop term is a 15–40% correction to γ_ν, largest at small R.

Checks and caveats. - IR poles cancel numerically in all colour structures; for C_RC_AT_Rn_f this requires combining quark and gluon final states. - The known LL ln²R² coefficient is reproduced. - The LL small-R approximation is poor even at very small R; a fit including the NLL lnR² term is good up to R∼0.4, where it overshoots by ~10%. This implies a large NLL small-R coefficient. - Results are numerical rather than analytic. - Coherence-violating effects are noted but enter only at five loops beyond leading N_c. - The provided text truncates before the phenomenological impact discussion.

The RSV subtraction strategy is pitched as reusable for other clustering-dependent three-loop soft functions.

item.title: CMS search for TT̅→(ϕt)(ϕt), ϕ→γγ, boosted all-hadronic tops
item.dc:creator: CMS Collaboration
item.description:
This is a substructure application rather than a methods paper. It uses 138 fb⁻¹ at 13 TeV.

Selection. - Two AK8 jets with p_T>350 GeV and soft-drop mass (β=0, z_cut=0.1) m_SD>50 GeV, with |Δη|<1.6. - Both jets ParticleNet top-tagged at the 0.5% light-jet mistag working point (~40% top efficiency). - Two photons; the signal region requires both to pass the WP80 identification, and a control region requires both to fail it.

Background estimate and fit. Background is extrapolated from the control region with an exponential transfer function in m_ϕ^reco. The fit is two-dimensional in (m_T^reco,m_ϕ^reco) over m_ϕ=100–300 GeV and m_T=800–1800 GeV.

Results. - The largest local excess is 2.7σ (1.5σ global) at m_T=900, m_ϕ=150 GeV. It is a single event against a predicted 7×10⁻⁶. - Upper limits are set on σ ℬ(T→ϕt)² ℬ_γγ(2-ℬ_γγ).

Jet-specific systematics. The analysis is statistics-dominated. The ParticleNet uncertainty has a 1.0% impact on r, and JES/JMS/JER/JMR are smaller still; FSR (3.0%) leads.

Caveats. - The second ϕ is left undecayed in simulation; the authors note this may slightly underestimate signal acceptance. - Jet–diphoton pairing is correct only 50–75% of the time (~40% at the lowest m_T). - Validation is statistically limited (VR p-value 0.14).

item.title: Unified description of longitudinal and transverse parton dynamics in cold nuclear matter
item.dc:creator: Weiyao Ke
item.description:
Relevance to this topic: This paper is only peripherally about jets. It concerns parton propagation in cold nuclear matter for SIDIS and Drell–Yan. The link to substructure is the final section on the one-point energy correlator (OPEC) in DIS.

What they did. Ke combines two strands of SCET_G work into one TMD-level matching coefficient, Eq. (1): - Longitudinal part. Impact-parameter-dependent medium-induced evolution M^med, building on Ke–Vitev’s RG analysis of collinear SIDIS. The coupled quark/gluon equations (2)–(3) are in the dilute limit υ ≃ α_s ρ_G L²/(4E) ≪ 1. They run over ξ² ≲ μ² ≲ min{2E/L, μ_b²}. Finite b therefore truncates the coherent-radiation window, so energy loss depends on the transverse resolution. - Transverse part. Broadening through the exponentiated Glauber cross section Σ_i(b,Y). - Fix to the collision kernel. The kernel is BFKL-evolved in rapidity, but leading-order BFKL “produces excessively strong radiative broadening.” It is tamed with a Kwieciński-type kinematical constraint (following Deak et al.) and a Kovchegov–Weigert-style running coupling.

Results. One parameter set (ρ_G = 0.5 fm⁻³, ξ² = 0.12 GeV²) reproduces the main trends of HERMES Xe/d multiplicity ratios and E866 Fe/Be and W/Be Drell–Yan ratios. The paper also gives EIC e+Pb/e+d predictions at √s = 60 GeV, Q² = 20 GeV², x_B = 0.1 and 0.4. Attenuation is stronger at x_B = 0.4, because the rest-frame parton energy E ≃ Q²/(2m_N x_B) is lower.

The jet-substructure-relevant point. Energy weighting kills the leading final-state energy-loss enhancement via the momentum sum rule. For the OPEC at √s = 141 GeV and 10 < Q < 15 GeV: - the dynamical cold-nuclear-matter correction is below 1% in the back-to-back region; - the roughly 30% nuclear modification comes from the nPDFs.

So for nuclear energy correlators, the final-state medium effect largely cancels at this order. This makes the OPEC an nPDF probe rather than a medium probe, and is worth knowing before interpreting eA energy-correlator data as jet quenching.

Caveats. - Proceedings-length text; data agreement is described only as “main trends,” with no fit quality quoted. - Vacuum nonperturbative TMD input is used, and in-nucleus hadronization is explicitly excluded. - The υ ≪ 1 limit is stretched at low-E HERMES and EIC kinematics.

item.title: New Observables for Resonant and Non-Resonant New Physics Searches at Colliders
item.dc:creator: Julien Touch\`eque
item.description:
This is a UCLouvain PhD thesis (Touchèque, supervised by Degrande). It is only tangential to substructure. The supplied text runs through the abstract, introduction and textbook SM material in Chapter 1, and is cut off before the analysis chapters. So the jet content below rests only on the abstract and chapter outline.

The relevant part is Chapter 4, which searches for top-philic colour-singlet and colour-octet scalars in four-top final states. It covers fully hadronic, leptonic and same-sign dileptonic channels, with signals generated at NLO QCD. The scalar decays yield boosted tt̅ pairs:

  • Hadronic tops are reconstructed with ML taggers for wide hadronic jets.
  • Leptonic tops are reconstructed assuming on-shell W decays.
  • Event selection uses a new scheme built on the invariant masses of top pairs.

The abstract claims limits improved by up to an order of magnitude over a recast CMS analysis. The underlying work is published (JHEP 11 (2025) 091, plus PRD 111 (2025) 055037), so there is nothing new here for substructure beyond packaging. If boosted multi-top tagging matters to you, read the JHEP paper directly.

Chapter 3, on CP-odd SMEFT triple-product asymmetries in WZ/Wγ, is unrelated to jets.

item.title: Probing jet quenching via the correlation of groomed jet substructure observables in Pb–Pb and pp collisions
item.dc:creator: ALICE Collaboration
item.description:
Setup. ALICE reports a fully corrected 2D (θ_g, z_g) measurement, unfolded with 3D iterative Bayesian unfolding in (p_T, z_g, θ_g). The sample is:

  • Charged R=0.2 anti-k_T jets with 60≤p_T,ch jet<80 GeV.
  • pp (18 nb⁻¹) and 0–10% Pb–Pb (0.12 nb⁻¹) at 5.02 TeV.
  • Soft Drop with z_cut=0.2, β=0; tagging fractions are 89% (pp) and 87% (Pb–Pb).
  • Projections in two bins: z_g split at 0.35, θ_g split at 0.3.

Results.

  • Narrowing: Pb–Pb jets are narrower in both z_g bins. The appendix double ratio is flat, so the narrowing is effectively z_g-independent once the yield shift is accounted for.
  • Narrow jets (θ_g<0.3): z_g shows no modification.
  • Wide jets (θ_g>0.3): the Pb/pp z_g ratio has a slope (less balanced in Pb–Pb). Relative to a constant of ≈0.82, the significance is 2.7σ statistical only and 2.0σ with systematics. It is limited by pp statistics.
  • pp generators: PYTHIA and POWHEG describe the data, while Herwig has too few wide jets.
  • Pb–Pb models:
  • JEWEL overestimates the narrowing.
  • JETSCAPE describes it well but over-depletes large θ_g for unbalanced jets.
  • The Hybrid model is insensitive to the wake. At large θ_g, unbalanced jets prefer the variant with elastic (Molière) scattering and balanced jets the variant without.

Caveats. Survival bias is not disentangled; the authors themselves point to the CMS γ-tagged R_g result. The aggressive grooming at small R kills sensitivity to medium response. Residual background mistags of 5–15% are handled via thermal non-closure.

The main advance is that this is the first correlated (θ_g, z_g) unfolding in AA. The physics signal, however, is a 2σ hint.

item.title: In medium evolution of the energy-energy correlators
item.dc:creator: Weiyao Ke
item.description:
These are Ke’s proceedings, summarising Ke–Meçaj–Vitev (JHEP 04 (2026) 155).

Framework. In SCET_G at first order in opacity, the regime is thin, dilute media with p_T/L≫α_sρ_G L∼m_D². The EEC jet function receives two kinds of medium correction:

  1. Non-contact fixed-order correction. It changes character at θ_LPM=√(8π/(p_T L)) and carries a Coulomb log. It depletes the EEC below θ_LPM and enhances it above.
  2. Medium-induced anomalous dimension. This is a matrix Γ^med(N) acting in the window Λ_QCD/p_T≪θ≪θ_LPM. Its strength is set by w_med=4πα_sρ_effL_eff²/(2p_T). The diagonal entries grow linearly in N, which motivates ratios of higher-point correlators to the EEC. Its effect is extra small-angle suppression, stronger for gluon jets.

The medium enters only through two path-integrated quantities, ρ_eff and L_eff; coherence means the local density profile is not resolved at this order. The switch from vacuum to modified evolution occurs at μ_m∼√(p_T/L_eff).

Phenomenology.

  • p–Pb: compared with preliminary ALICE minimum-bias data for R=0.4 jets in charged-jet p_T bins of 20–80 GeV. The calculation gives small-angle suppression that weakens with p_T, consistent with the data.
  • O–O: projections are given for O–O collisions at 5.36 TeV.

Caveats.

  • Charged jets are approximated by p_T^ch≃23 p_T^full, with no track functions.
  • The uncertainty bands vary only the matching scale, not the medium parameters.
  • Hadronization dominates at small θ, and recoil and medium response matter near θ∼R.

Connection to the ALICE paper. Both are probing medium-modified angular structure, but in opposite regimes. ALICE uses dense central Pb–Pb with hard grooming, where survival bias dominates. Ke works in the thin-medium limit, where a modified anomalous dimension is a cleaner, calculable target. The p_T and system-size scaling of w_med offers a falsifiable test that groomed z_g currently does not.

item.title: Non-global logarithms and fiducial transverse-momentum-dependent observables in deep-inelastic scattering
item.dc:creator: Shuo Lin et al.
item.description:
Lin and Zhou replace the lepton–jet imbalance with a jet-free fiducial imbalance, q_T = l′T + Σ{h∈|η|<Δη/2} p_hT. By momentum conservation this equals minus the total p_T outside the window, so the rapidity window plays the role of the jet boundary. At one loop, the jet-radius coefficients c₀(R), c₁(R) are replaced by analytic B₀(Δη) = −Δη − 2ln(1−e^{−Δη}) and B₁(Δη) = 4 atanh(e^{−Δη/2}) − 2e^{−Δη/2}. For reference, inclusive-k_T at R=1 gives c₀ = −0.253 and c₁ = 0.782.

The non-global treatment has three parts: - They derive closed-form two-loop angular coefficients I₀ and I₁ (dilogarithm expressions). - The azimuthal-average NGL U₀ is resummed at LL, large-N_c, with a BMS dipole-shower Monte Carlo using a 1 − J₀(bk_T) weight. - The cos φ harmonic NGL is kept only at O(α_s²). It is single-log, U₁⁽²⁾ ~ ᾱ_s² I₁ ln(P_T/μ_b), whereas U₀⁽²⁾ is double-log.

Headline numbers: - ⟨cos φ⟩ at q_T = 1 GeV roughly halves from Δη = 1 to Δη = 2. For HERA it goes 0.280 → 0.134 → 0.074 for Δη = 1, 2, 3. - At the EIC, |A_UT| and |A_LT| grow with Δη and peak near q_T ~ 1–1.5 GeV. - A_LT at Δη = 1 and q_T = 1 GeV is ≈0.25 at EicC versus ≈0.02 at EIC.

For this topic, the paper gives an algorithm-independent recoil-control knob with analytic boundary dependence. It is a direct comparator to the H1 ML-unfolded lepton-jet measurements, and scanning Δη within one dataset tests the global and non-global contributions together.

Caveats: - NGLs are LL and large-N_c only, and the first-harmonic NGL is not resummed. - The S_NP inputs are borrowed from Drell–Yan fits (halved). - Twist-3 evolution of T_F and g̃ is approximated by unpolarized DGLAP. - The calculation is at parton level, with no hadronization or detector acceptance effects.

item.title: Flavor-resolved four-fermion probes at the FCC-ee Z pole
item.dc:creator: Syuhei Iguro
item.description:
This paper is only tangential to jets. Jet flavor tagging is an enabling assumption, but the analysis is parton-level and has no jet definition; the author notes the ΔR_min = 0.2 cut must eventually become an IR-safe jet definition.

The physics: using Z → QQ̄ℓℓ (Q = b, c; ℓ = μ, τ) at 200 ab⁻¹, the author sets tree-level, interference-only 95% CL reaches on vector contact operators of (2.5, 2.7, 3.5, 3.6) TeV for bμ, bτ, cμ, cτ. These assume unit efficiency, and the reach scales as ε_rec^{1/4}. The main point is flavor resolution. The projected EWPO likelihood in the (C^{bτ}, C^{cτ}) plane has correlation ρ = −0.9999 and effectively constrains only C^{bτ} + 0.058 C^{cτ}. The four-body channels constrain the flat direction, giving combined reaches of Λ^{bτ} > 11.8 TeV and Λ^{cτ} > 3.2 TeV.

What matters for jets: - The optimal hardness cut is only 3–5 GeV, so this needs b/c tagging on soft jets in busy four-body topologies. The author explicitly flags this as unvalidated. - b↔c migration cannot be absorbed into a common efficiency factor.

item.title: Prompting Particle Physics: Tokenized Multi-modal Foundation Models for Combinatorially Many Tasks
item.dc:creator: Nilotpal Kakati et al.
item.description:
The authors tokenize seven per-jet modalities in COCOA single-jet events (88.9M train, median truth-jet p_T 46 GeV). Content features use residual VQ-VAEs and positions use 1024-bin (η, cos φ, sin φ); calorimeter cells enter as 8×8 patch images. The modalities are tracks, topoclusters, cells, HGPflow particles, truth particles, truth jet and per-cell charged fraction. One model is trained over all 1302 input→output subsets with ≤3 modalities on each side. There are two decoders: nanoHEP (GPT-2-style, autoregressive) and HEP4M (4M-style, parallel with cardinality heads).

The jet-relevant benchmark is particle flow (TK+CL→TP), scored against truth particles:

Model Jet p_T IQR Median response C2ST AUC
HGPflow 0.0754 0.986 0.902
nanoHEP-pflow 0.0733 0.978 0.691
HEP4M-pflow 0.0836 0.994 0.940

The C2ST is an event-conditioned set-transformer two-sample test. Its point is that HGPflow matches on aggregate jet metrics but its constituent cloud is easily separable from truth, which argues for particle-cloud-level validation beyond jet response.

  • Extra inputs help. Adding cells (TK+CL+CE) gives IQR 0.0704 and AUC 0.650.
  • Unseen four-input combination. TK+CL+RP+CE, never presented in training, reaches 0.0688.

Caveats: - Not substructure. The paper is about reconstructing and simulating jet constituents; no substructure observables are shown. - Multi-task gain is small. On the benchmark itself, nanoHEP-multi (0.0781) is slightly worse than nanoHEP-pflow; at matched steps, from-scratch training gives 0.0758. - Truth-jet-input row is not a fair comparison. The 0.0305 IQR uses the truth jet as an input. - Refinement fails. RP→TP does not improve on the HGPflow input. - Cell generation fails. Generated cells are fully separable from truth (AUC 0.998), and the cell tokenizer round trip alone is separable at 0.96. - HEP4M artefacts. It needs cos/sin renormalisation and under-produces high topocluster multiplicities. - Simplified setup. The detector is simplified, tracks are parameterised fast simulation, and pileup is not discussed.

item.title: The era of charmed resonance searches at the LHC
item.dc:creator: Daniel Whiteson
item.description:
This is a flavour-tagging projection. The author starts from the ATLAS 139 fb⁻¹ untagged dijet spectrum and builds c-tagged background spectra using: - Pythia dijet flavour-pair fractions binned in (p_T, p_T), validated against ATLAS 7 TeV flavour-fraction data with a small +0.0073 bℓ correction. - GN2 c-tag efficiencies, interpolated log-linearly in p_T between the two published p_T samples. - A multi-hadron efficiency enhancement with α = 1.96, fitted to the observed b-tagged spectra.

Exclusive 1-tag and 2-tag categories are fitted jointly with four-parameter dijet functions. The limit-setting machinery reproduces ATLAS limits to within 10%.

Results: - Z′→cc̄. At ε_c = 0.6, the tagged search beats the inclusive one (gain G > 1) over the whole 2–4 TeV range, with roughly ±10% band dominated by the tagging model. - T→cg. The gain appears only at lower masses. - Doubling the inclusive sensitivity needs ε_ℓ = 0.12 at ε_c = 0.6 (current 0.15, a factor 1.3). At ε_c = 0.3 it needs 0.016 (current 0.083, a factor 5). - Perfect-tagger ceilings are G ≈ 8 (Z′) and G ≈ 2.2 (T).

The conclusion for tagger development is to optimise the loose working points.

Two points are of interest for jet physics: - Gluon splitting in the background. The multi-hadron fraction from g→cc̄ rises with p_T and is larger for charm than for bottom, and FSR scale variation moves the charm fraction f_c by +22/−14% at about 1.5 TeV. - IRC-safe flavour. Under IRC-safe interleaved flavour neutralisation (IFN), about 50% of cone-labelled charm jets become light at low mass. At 4–5.4 TeV only 17% stay charm. This reclassifies which jets count as charm but does not change the predicted tagged spectrum.

Caveats: there are no published p_T-differential c-tag efficiencies, so these are extrapolated. The 13 TeV flavour fractions are extrapolated from simulation (7 TeV data only reach p_T < 500 GeV). The analysis uses binary thresholds only.

item.title: Factorization and virtuality evolution of jet functions in heavy-ion collisions
item.dc:creator: Carlos Lamas et al.
item.description:
The provided full text is truncated at the start of Sec. III, so only the formalism is covered here; the numerical results come from the abstract only.

For γ+jet production in AA collisions, the authors model the nuclei as Glauber ensembles of uncorrelated nucleons. They derive an impact-parameter-dependent factorized cross section: thickness beam functions, times the on-shell 2→2 partonic cross section, convolved with an in-medium jet function 𝒥_k(p_I; p_J, X). The jet function explicitly retains the initial virtuality m_I² = p_I², defined in a physical gauge, with quark and gluon projectors fixed by Ward identities.

They then set up BDMPS-Z Feynman rules for this object: - dressed propagators as path integrals with Wilson lines; - a harmonic-oscillator dipole approximation; - a soft-gluon emission vertex; - a new single-line color-survival factor, exp(−½∫dt/λ_R), controlled by the light-cone mean free path λ_R.

Per the abstract: - Integrating over m_I² recovers standard BDMPS-Z p_⊥ broadening and the soft medium-induced spectrum. - The ratio of medium formation time τ₀ to jet formation time controls which initial virtualities contribute. Vacuum radiation dominates when the jet forms well before τ₀. - As τ₀ → 0, the mean free path becomes the controlling scale instead.

This matters for pre-equilibrium quenching and small systems, and offers a formalism-independent object for comparing energy-loss models. The authors frame it as a common ground for the spread in q̂ extractions.

Caveats: - Neglected couplings. Medium couplings to initial-state partons are dropped, justified only at lowest order; couplings to the hard vertex are argued to be subleading. - Limited order. The hard process is LO, and the NLO part is soft-gluon only, for quark jets. - Approximations. The calculation uses the eikonal limit for the leading parton and the harmonic-oscillator approximation. - No dynamical evolution. The authors state that the full virtuality evolution of the shower through the medium is not described dynamically.

item.title: Optimizing Cell-Based Negative Weight Mitigation with Optimal Transport
item.dc:creator: Lauren Hay et al.
item.description:
This paper replaces the modified-Euclidean metric in Andersen–Maier cell resampling with IRC-safe OT metrics: event-level EMD in (η,φ) with p_T weights, and the spectral EMD (SEMD). A negative-weight seed grows a hypersphere in metric space until the enclosed net weight is positive, then weights are redistributed as w_i → (Σw/Σ|w|)|w_i|.

The test sample is MG5_aMC@NLO+Pythia 8.3 Z+jets at 13 TeV, with 37.6% negative weights and O(10⁵) events. The reweight fraction is set deliberately high at f_RW = 0.75. Findings: - β choice: β = 1 and 0.5 give the least bias. β = 1 was chosen on cost grounds. - Stage: resampling after hadronization beats parton-shower and Born-level resampling. - Metric comparison: EMD ≳ SEMD, both better than the original metric, most visibly in H_T and leading-jet p_T. - ΣMD: the distance to the original sample stays below the sample’s statistical uncertainty (δσ/σ = 0.0127). - Statistical gain: all variants take 1/f_ESS from 16 to 6. The metric therefore controls bias, not the statistical gain.

For jets specifically, the relevant change is that IRC safety comes from the metric itself. The previous jet-clustering step, and its dependence on algorithm and R, is no longer needed. Jets otherwise enter only as anti-k_t R = 0.4 validation observables, so this is not a substructure paper.

Caveats: - This is proceedings-length and the evidence is mostly histogram comparisons. - Only one low-statistics sample is tested. - The ΣMD figure of merit (arXiv:2609.30418) uses the EMD as its ground metric. That may flatter the EMD-based resampler relative to the Euclidean baseline; this is my inference, not addressed by the authors.

item.title: Parnassus for the CLD Detector: A Generative ML Surrogate for Detector Simulation and Reconstruction at the FCC-ee
item.dc:creator: Umar Sohail Qureshi et al.
item.description:
Model. A two-stage conditional flow-matching surrogate for CLD_o2_v07 Geant4 + PandoraPFA, trained on Z→qq̄ (u,d) and bb̄ at 91.2 GeV: - An event-level MLP models N, H_T and missing-momentum components. - A cross-attention DiT (~5M parameters) generates the particles, each with species and d₀, z₀ and their significances. - Conditioning includes the truth production vertex, which is what lets it reproduce displaced heavy-flavour tails. - cc̄ and ss̄ are held out as out-of-distribution tests.

Jet-level results. After Durham exclusive 2-jet clustering, Parnassus beats Delphes on every observable and every metric. Examples: - Jet mass: W₁ = 0.247 vs 1.886 for Delphes. - e₂^(β=2): VLC 0.076 vs 0.865. - m_jj: VLC 0.52 vs 58.6.

Flavour tagging. A transformer tagger (b/c/s/q) trained on surrogate output gives: - Accuracy 0.684 vs 0.693 for full simulation. - b-vs-c mistag at 80% efficiency: 1.58% vs 1.00%, a ~60% relative excess. - Delphes overestimates separability (accuracy 0.732; b-vs-c mistag 0.24%). - A full-sim-trained tagger drops only 0.012 in accuracy when applied to Parnassus.

Speed. 1.3 ms/event on an A100 and 39 ms on a CPU core, vs 6.0 s for full simulation and reconstruction.

This is a credible e⁺e⁻ jet-flavour benchmark. It shows directly that Delphes-based tagging projections are optimistic.

Caveats: - Coordinates and substructure definitions (p_T, ΔR girth) are carried over from the CMS setup rather than e⁺e⁻-native variables; the authors acknowledge this. - Hyperparameters are untuned from the CMS configuration. - bb̄ reproduces worse than the held-out flavours. - The HitPF extension is qualitative and shows impact-parameter deviations. - No boosted or multi-prong substructure is tested.

item.title: Impact of soft QCD effects over intrajet azimuthal anisotropies
item.dc:creator: Jesus Alberto V. Corral et al.
item.description:
This is a generator-level reinterpretation of the CMS intrajet v₂ measurement (arXiv:2312.17103), using PYTHIA 8.309 with the Monash, CP5 and QCD-scheme CR tunes. The setup is anti-kT R=0.8 jets with pT>550 GeV and |η|<1.6, particles with 0.3<j_T<3 GeV, and a long-range cut |Δη*|>2.

Tune spectra: CP5 gives a softer N_ch spectrum (inclusive ⟨N_ch⟩ 27.3, vs 31.2 for Monash and 30.0 for QCD-CR), with fewer jets at high N_ch.

v₂ agreement with data (χ²/ndof):

Model N_ch < 80 N_ch ≥ 80
QCD-scheme CR 0.32 10.21
Sherpa (from CMS) 1.02 21.93
Monash 2.28 10.20
CP5 4.69 23.55

The high-N_ch excess persists for all tunes. The authors frame QCD-CR and Monash as “consistent at 2.3σ” in the top bin. That framing sits awkwardly with χ²/ndof ≈ 10 over those two points, and should not be read as agreement.

The new ingredient is rotating into the WTA-axis frame: - WTA lowers v₂ at the lowest N_ch for all tunes. - At high N_ch, Monash and CP5 shift away from their E-scheme values, while QCD-CR is the most frame-stable. - The authors tie the Monash shift to ⟨η*⟩ differences (2.08 for E-scheme vs 2.12 for WTA, at N_ch>80).

This argues that part of the high-N_ch “signal” is sensitive to soft-recoil effects on the jet axis, and it motivates a WTA-frame measurement.

Caveats: - No detector simulation. - The WTA predictions have no data to compare against. - The fit uses only three Fourier terms. - Differences between tunes are attributed to colour reconnection, but CP5 also differs in its ISR, FSR, MPI and α_s settings.

item.title: Event-Level Classification of Boosted Multi-Tau Signatures in scNMSSM Di-Higgs Production
item.dc:creator: Marwa Telba
item.description:
The signal is h₁h₁→4a₁→8τ with m_a₁=8.2 GeV (γ≈7.5, ΔR_ττ≈0.27), with Z(→ττ)+jet at pT^ττ>100 GeV as the main background. It is simulated with MG5+Pythia8+Delphes, using R=0.8 fat jets with the threshold lowered from 200 to 30 GeV. Without that change only 18% of signal events contain any fat jet.

Negative result for jet substructure. Standard two-prong discriminants fail against a background that is itself a ditau jet: - The separation power is S=0.016 for m_J and 0.09 for τ₂₁. - Neutrino losses (Z) and soft contamination (a₁) push both jet-mass distributions to about 18 GeV, despite parents at 8.2 and 91 GeV. - The best single variables are z_sub (S=0.36) and τ₁ (0.33). Normalising into τ₂₁ throws away information. - Energy correlation functions were not available from Delphes.

Performance (AUC):

Configuration AUC ε_S at ε_B=10%
Single-jet BDT vs Z 0.759 —
Event-level (32 inputs) vs Z 0.941 82%
Event-level vs tt̄→bb̄ττ 0.855 —
Cross-section-weighted combination 0.908 71%
  • The event-level gain is driven by fat-jet multiplicity and the soft-drop masses of the second and third jets.
  • tt̄ mimics the multiplicity and subleading masses; discrimination against it relies on N_τ and E_T^miss instead.
  • tt̄ makes up 66% of the surviving background at ε_B=1%, despite being under a quarter of the combined background cross section.

Caveats: - A str

item.title: Towards Foundation Models on Hardware Accelerators for Particle Physics
item.dc:creator: Maya Benyas et al.
item.description:
The authors distil the 423M-parameter OmniLearned-Large model into Deep Sets students on the standard Pythia+Delphes top-tagging dataset (p_T 550–650 GeV). The teacher was pretrained on >1B jets across 210 classes, then fine-tuned to AUC 0.9880 and 1/ϵ_B = 3365 at ϵ_S = 30%. The distillation loss uses α = β = 0.5 and T = 4.

Results at 30% signal efficiency:

Change Rejection
Adding one message-passing layer (logm_ij, logΔR_ij, logk_T,ij on the top-64 constituents; 11k → 17k params) 748 → 1980
Distillation vs. hard-label cross-entropy (same student) 1216 → 1980
Distilling from the pretrained teacher vs. a from-scratch teacher of the same architecture 1020 → 1980

Accuracy moves by only ~0.2–0.3 points across these comparisons, so the pretraining benefit sits almost entirely in the ROC tail. The pretrained teacher itself has ~4× better rejection than its from-scratch counterpart, and roughly half of that gain survives into the student. This is the first demonstration that the pretraining benefit, not just the teacher’s capacity, transfers through distillation. The best student reaches 93.98% accuracy versus 94.38% for OmniLearned-Small, with 155× fewer parameters.

Quantization: - Post-training quantization at 8 bits is destructive: 59% accuracy for the message-passing student, and chance level at 4 bits. - Quantization-aware training at 8 bits (Brevitas) recovers 93.95% accuracy and 1787 rejection.

Caveats: - No HLS/FPGA synthesis, latency or resource numbers yet. - The message-passing student costs 14.3M MACs per jet versus 305k for plain Deep Sets. That 47× gap is what will matter against a µs-scale trigger budget, and the paper does not yet address it. - There is a single hyperparameter point, and K = 64 was not optimized. - Only the saturated top-tagging benchmark is tested.

item.title: Search for boosted VBS W^±W^±H production with same-sign leptons and b-jets
item.dc:creator: ATLAS Collaboration
item.description:
First ATLAS search for EW W^±W^±Hjj, targeting the quartic WWHH coupling via κ_WW. The physics result is a null: observed (expected) 95% CL exclusion of κ_WW outside [-2.1,4.1] ([-1.9,3.9]), statistically limited (data stat impact 0.22 vs total 0.26 on μ for the κ_WW=-2 benchmark). Weaker than the recent CMS inclusive VVH result (κ_2V∈[0.4,1.6]), but a different channel.

For substructure, the interesting content is the analysis architecture. The boosted H→bb̅ candidate is a single anti-k_t R=1.0 jet built from UFOs (Track-CaloClusters), groomed with Soft-Drop + Constituent Subtraction + SoftKiller, 250<p_T<3000 GeV, m_J>40 GeV. Tagging uses GN2X, the transformer H→bb/cc/QCD tagger, with the discriminant in Eq. (1) at f_Hcc=0.02; the working point is a mass-flat 1.55% multijet mistag, giving ~80% H→bb efficiency. Notably, GN2X calibration is a leading systematic — flavor tagging (signal) contributes 0.050 to the μ impact, second only to the fake-factor uncertainty (0.084) and well above jet energy/mass scale (0.014). The VBS forward-jet topology is captured by an RNN tagger on small-R four-momenta (VBF-RNN) rather than cut-based m_jj/Δη_jj, retaining ~80% signal at score >0.2, and explicitly excludes small-R jets within ΔR<1.4 of the large-R Higgs candidate. This is a clean demonstration that mass-decorrelated boosted-X→bb taggers plus ML VBS tagging are now the default toolkit for rare EW processes; the caveat is that at these yields (9 observed, 12.5 expected background) the boosted approach is entirely statistics-limited and the resolved topology added negligible sensitivity.

item.title: Exact Amplitude Reconstruction in the Real Common-Phase Sector of Small-x Diffractive Energy Flow
item.dc:creator: Sanskriti Agrawal et al.
item.description:
This is a formal small-x/EIC tomography paper; the jet connection runs through energy-flow operators and coherent diffractive dijet production rather than jet substructure in the collider-QCD sense. The authors set up an operator-level map from the impact-parameter-dependent dipole amplitude T_Y(r,b,ϕ) (C-even, real, even cosine harmonics T_2n) to the gluon Wigner harmonics W_2n (via a rotationally diagonal Bessel transform, ∝∫r dr J_2n(kr)T̃_2n) and to the longitudinal-photon diffractive dijet amplitude harmonics A_2n∝∫∫ψ_L T_2n J_2n(Pr)J_2n(Δb). Their central claim: in the Born leading-eikonal, longitudinal, C-even sector all harmonics share a common overall phase, so A_2n/A_0∈ℝ, and in a node-free bin the normalized amplitude is recovered exactly as √(p_E(θ)), with harmonic ratios from a direct Fourier projection (Eq. 25). For generic complex amplitudes the energy-flow intensity only yields autocorrelations s_N=∑_l a_l+Na_l^* — the standard phase-retrieval non-uniqueness.

The genuinely new content for energy-flow observables: they treat the diffractive dijet energy-flow distribution as an intensity and give an explicit deconvolution (generating function X(t)=√(1+𝒞(t)), plus a logarithmic/cumulant representation) that systematically subtracts reducible lower-harmonic mixing — e.g. clarifying that the measured cos4ϕ moment contains 2x_2+x_1², so the “true” A_4 requires subtracting the elliptic x_1². Caveats are stated forthrightly: the common-phase property is not an all-order theorem — nodes leave a sign ambiguity, odderon/C-odd exchange, dispersive real-part corrections with harmonic-dependent slopes λ_2n, and 𝒪(α_s) radiation all break it. No numerical EIC projections are given; this is a formalism/feasibility paper.

item.title: Multitask Jet Analysis with Vision-Language Models: A Physics-Informed Four-Panel Representation
item.dc:creator: Lu Zhang et al.
item.description:
Squarely on jet tagging/substructure, but the novelty is representational rather than physics-reach. Each JetClass jet is rendered as a 224×224 RGB image of four aligned (Δη,Δϕ) panels encoding: (P1) p_T flow all/charged/neutral; (P2) charged-hadron/neutral-hadron/EM composition; (P3) p_T-weighted transverse and longitudinal impact-parameter significances plus displaced-track multiplicity (s≥2); (P4) signed-track p_T densities and local p_T^κ-weighted (κ=0.5) jet-charge asymmetry. Jets are canonicalized (centroid, PCA rotation for a_PCA≥0.05, deterministic reflections), Gaussian-deposited (σ=0.03) and log-compressed. Four open VLMs are LoRA-adapted for three tasks (10-class tagging, 6-field attribute prediction, panel-consistency/localization).

Results: zero-shot is at chance (3.33–10.57% macro recall); after adaptation on 200k jets (0.2% of JetClass) Gemma4-E4B hits 75.05% macro recall / 74.87% F_1, 93.31% Task-2 field-mean, 99.88%/99.75% consistency/localization. Panel ablations are the physics-relevant payoff: relative to p_T-flow alone (57.50%), adding species→61.29%, then displacement→67.47% (the dominant handle, via b/c lifetime), while jet-charge (P4) specifically lifts the near-degenerate hadronic Z→qq̅ (Zqq 22.5→34.2%). Fixed-budget WZ reallocation buys up to +9.83 pts on Zqq at ~constant macro recall. Transfer to JetClass-II and real-data Aspen Open Jets holds (>70% Task 1, >92% Task 2/3 with 3k target jets). Caveat, stated by the authors: this is not competitive with ParticleTransformer/ParticleNet on discrimination — 75% 10-class recall is well below dedicated taggers — and the appeal is a single instruction-conditioned multitask interface, not raw performance. Pixelization also discards constituent-level information by construction.

item.title: PSICHE: Probabilistic, Structure-Intrinsic Clustering with a Hierarchical Embedding
item.dc:creator: Margaret Lazarovits et al.
item.description:
This introduces a jet clustering algorithm that abandons fixed cone size and fixed multiplicity, instead learning both jointly. The core is a variational Gaussian mixture model (vGMM) embedded inside Bayesian Hierarchical Clustering: BHC handles jet-level associations via tree-consistent merges (restricted to Voronoi/Delaunay nearest neighbors, giving N ln N scaling as in FastJet), while each embedded vGMM models subcluster substructure. Key design choices for substructure: energy-proportional data weights ωₙ = ω·Eₙ preserve four-vector sums (Eqs. 10–11) and give IRC safety at jet level; a subcluster-inheritance + L2-overlap-based merge scheme regulates subcluster multiplicity and provides “IRC protection” at subcluster level (tested by injecting ghost subclusters, none survive). The transfer factor ω = 4 GeV acts as a soft lower resolution bound rather than a hard cone. Notably, PSICHE clusters in space and time (η, φ, t), natively ingesting per-cell measurement precisions Λ*ₙ matched to simulated energy/timing resolutions (σ_t ≈ 100 ps beam spread, CMS-ECAL-like geometry).

Concrete results: on Pythia 8.3 dijets it reproduces AK4/8/15 multiplicity and jet mass/energy/time spectra; on tt̄ it dynamically shrinks jet size ∝ m_jet/p_T, recovering a W/top admixture that no single AK radius captures. On single boosted W it consistently finds two-subcluster structure where a vGMM seeded on AK constituents fails to regulate multiplicity.

For this topic, the significance is a fully unsupervised, probabilistic framework that unifies clustering and substructure resolution with timing and experimental uncertainties — a genuinely different paradigm from sequential recombination + grooming. Caveats: the Λ* addition breaks inverse-Wishart conjugacy (handled approximately); the subcluster IRC argument is empirical, not proven; benchmarks are idealized single-detector simulation, and the pileup-mitigation demonstration is only sketched (text truncated). No timing/throughput numbers versus FastJet are given.

item.title: Cat's Cradle diagrams for substructure studies
item.dc:creator: Peter Skands
item.description:
Skands proposes a bookkeeping/visualization framework (“cat’s cradle diagrams”) plotting the parametric size αₛ^A L^λ of each perturbative coefficient versus a p_T-like substructure resolution scale, for a back-to-back qq̄ dipole at √s = 200 GeV (α_s = 0.11). The physics point: in the “resolved jet substructure” region (roughly 5 ≲ p_T ≲ 20 GeV here), neither fixed-order (N^nLO) nor soft-collinear (N^nLL) power counting gives systematic convergence — each delivers only ~half an effective order per full order (Eqs. 9–10 define R_acc and n_eff = log_{αₛ} R_acc). He introduces an intermediate counting N^nLJ, assigning terms with equal 3A−2λ the same order, nested as N^nLO ⊂ N^nLJ ⊂ N^{n+1}LL, with 1/3-order increments.

The concrete claim for substructure: conventional LL p_T-ordered dipole/antenna showers (Pythia, Vincia defaults) actually include the αₛL term beyond pure LL (Eq. 12/15), making them “LJ+LL” accurate — about an order of magnitude better than pure LL resummation across the resolved-substructure region, with a broad plateau of constant n_eff. Azimuthal averaging further compensates the local-recoil αₛ²L² violation by a factor ~1/3 (2/3 vs 1/3 random-walk argument), keeping angular-averaged observables near NLL down to a few GeV. Matrix-element corrections extend this to NLO+LJ+LL, flat over the whole range.

For this topic it offers a quantitative language for what “substructure accuracy” means midway between hard and soft regimes — useful for judging shower/grooming accuracy claims. Appendix A gives exact Z→qgq̄ Ariadne-p_T Sudakov integrals and shows running-coupling coefficients stay O(1) with ~20% per-order growth. Caveats the author states plainly: exponent-level only (not cross-section), one-prong observable tuned to the shower ordering variable, order-unity coefficient assumption tested only at lowest order, final-state qq̄ dipole only, and he explicitly claims no new physics results — the diagrams and N^nLJ counting are the deliverable, and N^nLJ is close to existing double-log counting.

item.title: The production of bottom-flavoured jets at the LHC through bottom-quark pair production at NNLO+PS
item.dc:creator: Rhorry Gauld et al.
item.description:
Watchlist hit (jet algorithms, flavour tagging) — abstract only, not yet read for a briefing.

We consider the dominant production mechanism of bottom-flavoured jets at the LHC, which proceeds through bottom-quark pair production. We compute next-to-next-to- leading-order (NNLO) QCD corrections retaining full bottom-quark mass effects and match them with a parton shower (NNLO+PS). Our predictions provide a realistic description of events with one and two bottom-flavoured jets at both the partonic and hadronic level. We compare different jet-flavour definitions and confirm that the dominant numerical differences between the jet algorithms result from the treatment of jets that contain two bottom quarks originating from g→bb̅ splittings. We compare our predictions, using the experimental bottom-flavour tagging prescription, with measurements by ATLAS, CMS, and LHCb at 7 and 13 TeV, finding good agreement for the distributions presented by ATLAS and CMS and a good description of the shapes of the LHCb data. We also discuss the impact of various physics effects on the considered distributions: power corrections in the bottom-quark mass, the implications of symmetric/asymmetric jet-selection cuts, as well as contributions from multi-parton interactions.

item.title: Baryon-to-meson ratios in the Lund jet plane: resolving string-junction and thermal-fragmentation effects
item.dc:creator: Robert Vertesi
item.description:
Watchlist hit (Lund plane, Lund jet plane) — abstract only, not yet read for a briefing.

Baryon-to-meson ratios inside charged jets are studied in the Lund jet plane using PYTHIA simulations of pp collisions at √(s) = 14 TeV, with 15 < p_T^ch,jet < 30 GeV/c in an acceptance compatible with the future ALICE 3 detector. Jets are reclustered with the Cambridge–Aachen algorithm and identified hadrons are tagged at the splitting where they first separate from the leading branch. Three model configurations are compared: Monash, color reconnection beyond leading color (CR-BLC), and CR-BLC combined with thermodynamical string fragmentation (Thermal+CR-BLC). The Λ_c⁺/D⁰ ratio rises with log(1/z) in the two configurations that include color-string junctions and is approximately flat under Monash. The same trend is present at the first Cambridge–Aachen branching, indicating that the effect is set at the level of the color topology rather than through the cumulative action of many soft splittings. Light- and strange-sector ratios show no z-dependent signature of either mechanism, but the angular projection reveals non-trivial structure at the first branching that is washed out when emissions are summed. The Cambridge–Aachen declustering and the Lund plane together separate the kinematic signatures of the two baryon-enhancement mechanisms in PYTHIA and provide observables accessible to future ALICE 3 measurements.

item.title: From Nuclear Many-Body Correlations to Energy Detector Correlators
item.dc:creator: Jo\~{a}o Barata et al.
item.description:
Watchlist hit (energy flow) — abstract only, not yet read for a briefing.

Relativistic nuclear collisions have opened an experimental arena for studying many-body correlations in nuclear ground states. However, the connection between initial-state correlations and final-state multi-particle observables measured at colliders is not yet formulated as a systematically improvable matching problem. We show that detector correlators built from asymptotic energy flows provide a natural framework for realizing such a construction. In particular, we express the asymptotic energy flow as a functional of the early-time stress tensor, and expand it in suitable modes to recover the familiar linear hydrodynamic relations at leading order. Then, motivated by small-x QCD, we map angular projections of detector correlators to multipole-operator correlators computed in the colliding nuclei. We thus establish a systematic formalism for matching long-wavelength correlations between incoming and outgoing QCD states in high-energy hadronic collisions.

item.title: PSICHE: Probabilistic, Structure-Intrinsic Clustering with Hierarchical Embedding for Jet Reconstruction
item.dc:creator: Margaret Lazarovits et al.
item.description:
A genuinely new clustering paradigm rather than a substructure measurement. PSICHE embeds a variational Gaussian mixture model (vGMM) inside Bayesian Hierarchical Clustering, so that jet multiplicity/scale (tree level) and internal substructure (mixture level) are inferred jointly and unsupervised, with no pre-set cone size or prong count. Key novelties for substructure: (i) dynamically learned, variable jet sizes; (ii) simultaneous multi-scale learning of subclusters; (iii) clustering in space and time (η,φ,t), with per-cell energy/time measurement precisions Λ*_n folded directly into the likelihood; (iv) energy-proportional data weights ω_n=ω·E_n that give jet-level IRC safety and preserve four-vector sums. Subcluster proliferation is controlled by hierarchical inheritance (child multiplicity seeded to sum of parents) plus explicit pairwise merge comparisons via L2 Gaussian overlap. Nearest-neighbor (Voronoi/Delaunay, FastJet 3.4-based) merge restriction brings scaling to ~N ln N.

Concrete substructure results: on boosted single-W samples PSICHE consistently resolves the two-prong parton structure as two subclusters, where a vGMM run post-hoc on AK-jet constituents fails to regulate multiplicity. In tt̄, it dynamically reconstructs both resolved and boosted top/W jets, tracking jet size ∝ m_jet/p_T across p̂_T^min=200→500 GeV, whereas AK jets impose hard cone cutoffs. A top-jet decomposes into three localized prongs (bb + W→qq) plus a dispersive soft-radiation component. The hyperparameter ω (=4 GeV here) softly sets the resolved scale — this replaces the cone parameter but is not eliminated. Validation is against anti-k_T (R=0.4/0.8/1.5) on Pythia 8.3 + idealized CMS-ECAL-like calo/PF simulation; there is no comparison yet to standard substructure taggers (N-subjettiness, soft drop) or performance under realistic detector/BIB effects. The time dimension enabling new time-based substructure observables (subcluster times, space-time covariance) is the most distinctive extension for the field.

item.title: Generalized Detectors at Colliders
item.dc:creator: Mark Gonzalez et al.
item.description:
Watchlist hit (energy correlators, jet functions, infrared and collinear safe) — abstract only, not yet read for a briefing.

Recent progress in collider physics has reformulated phenomenological questions in terms of detector correlation functions and advanced their theoretical understanding. These advances have primarily focused on correlators of the average null energy operator, ℰ(n⃗), known as energy correlators. However, colliders have access to a much broader class of detector operators, ℰⁿ_R(n⃗), which measure powers of the energy on a subset of hadrons R, such as charged hadrons. These generalized detectors are generically not infrared and collinear safe, and their description requires nonperturbative matching between the hadronic detectors measured in the infrared and the partonic detectors used in ultraviolet calculations. We develop a framework for computing their multi-point correlation functions. We introduce universal nonperturbative matching coefficients, termed “detector functions”, that implement this infrared-ultraviolet matching. For the ℰ_Rⁿ operators studied here, these coefficients are represented by energy-weighted moments of single- and multi-hadron fragmentation functions. We present their renormalization group structure, derive QCD factorization theorems for the projected correlators, and compute jet functions through next-to-leading order. In the fixed-coupling pure Yang-Mills limit, we derive the light-ray OPE of hadronic detectors and connect it to the QCD factorization framework. We also identify universal nonperturbative power corrections generated by soft radiation, which are enhanced in the collinear limit and can substantially modify the perturbative angular scaling. A parton shower study finds qualitative agreement with the predicted perturbative and nonperturbative scaling behaviors. Our work significantly broadens the space of detector operators under theoretical control, with potential phenomenological applications.

item.title: Top-quark pair production sensitivity to heavy new physics at the FCC-ee
item.dc:creator: Jacopo De Piccoli et al.
item.description:
Watchlist hit (flavour tagging, jet flavour) — abstract only, not yet read for a briefing.

We study the sensitivity of top-quark pair production at the FCC-ee to heavy new physics, parametrised in the Standard Model effective field theory, using discriminants based on matrix elements. The analysis includes detector reconstruction effects, obtained with a fast simulation of the IDEA detector concept, and jet flavour tagging. We consider dimension-six operators that modify the electroweak couplings of the top quark or generate four-fermion interactions, at leading order and in diagrams with two resonant top quarks. The full six-body kinematic information is employed to maximise the discrimination power against the Standard Model. Two bins per dimension in the space of 12 discriminants, one per operator considered, provide a simple and robust methodology to set nearly optimal multidimensional constraints. Bounds on the new physics scale can reach values up to 30 TeV in a single-operator fit and up to 5 TeV in a global multi-operator fit. A combination with High-Luminosity LHC prospects on top-quark operators shows complementary sensitivities which help lift approximate degeneracies.

item.title: Probing Local Charm Hadronization Dynamics with Hadron-Anchored Energy Correlators
item.dc:creator: Robert Vertesi
item.description:
Watchlist hit (energy correlator, energy correlators, energy flow) — abstract only, not yet read for a briefing.

We introduce the hadron-anchored energy correlator (HAEC), a jet-restricted realization of the fragmentation energy correlator and the semi-inclusive energy correlator frameworks, and apply it to heavy-flavor-tagged jets in hadron collisions. Using \textsc{Pythia}~8 simulations of D⁰- and Λ_c⁺-tagged jets, we find a pronounced, localized suppression of energy flow around the Λ_c⁺ relative to the D⁰, followed by a sharp transition scaling as θ_0∝1/p_T^jet with little tune dependence. The conventional jet-axis radial profile shows qualitatively different color-reconnection dependence, suggesting reduced sensitivity of HAEC to jet-axis effects. A beauty-sector study can distinguish a heavy-quark-mass origin from a local fragmentation-vertex origin.

item.title: Flavor Flux Correlators, Forward-Backward Asymmetries, and Anomalies
item.dc:creator: Kyle Lee et al.
item.description:
Watchlist hit (energy correlators) — abstract only, not yet read for a briefing.

Flavor plays a crucial role in the structure of the Standard Model. As such, many important collider physics measurements incorporate the flavor information of detected hadrons. Recent progress in the study of energy correlators has enabled collider physics measurements of energy flux to be reformulated as operator statements. In this Letter, we introduce flavor flux correlators, which measure the angular distribution and correlations of flavor quantum numbers. We emphasize a unique feature of heavy flavor flux correlators as compared to correlators of other charges, namely the b and c flavor quantum numbers are gapped at the heavy quark mass scale, making them a particularly clean perturbative observables, with 𝒪(Λ_QCD/m_Q) suppressed non-perturbative power corrections. As an application, we reformulate the heavy quark forward-backward asymmetry as a macroscopic consequence of a mixed electroweak anomaly of the heavy-quark flavor current. Using the relation to the anomaly, we compute the flavor flux correlator analytically at next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order and verify using parton shower simulations that non-perturbative corrections are suppressed, as expected from the gapped nature of the heavy flavor quantum numbers. Flavor flux correlators can be measured using archival electron-positron collision data, as well as at Belle II and future colliders.

item.title: Semi-visible Jets from Sneaky Dark Matter
item.dc:creator: Deepak Kar et al.
item.description:
Watchlist hit (semi-visible jet, semi-visible jets) — abstract only, not yet read for a briefing.

In this paper, we compare two different ways of generating semi-visible jet signature in non-resonant production mode, and flag the potential advantages of the new generation approach we propose. In addition, we suggest a more efficient matrix element to parton shower matching configuration for this hadronic final state signature. Finally, we perform a reinterpretation study of the ATLAS search for t-channel semi-visible jet production and obtain collider limits on the sneaky DM scenario.

item.title: Learning the Geometry of Collider Events with Metric-Aware Deep Sets
item.dc:creator: Lauren Hay et al.
item.description:
Watchlist hit (particle flow) — abstract only, not yet read for a briefing.

Optimal transport gives structured data a geometry, but exact evaluation is costly in large pairwise analyses that exploit relationships among distances. Learned surrogates are faster, but need not preserve this metric structure. We develop a Deep Sets surrogate for OT between variable-size weighted point clouds that enforces non-negativity, exchange symmetry, and zero self-distance, leaving the triangle inequality unconstrained. Applied to the Energy Mover’s Distance between collider events in a particle physics application, the Metric-Aware Particle Flow Network achieves percent-level mean absolute percentage error while significantly improving inference throughput over other exact and approximate methods surveyed. The architectural constraints are found to improve properties that are not explicitly enforced: across 10⁶ held-out event triplets, triangle-inequality violations fall from 199 for a matched unconstrained network to 2, and the maximum from 149.5 to 5.8 GeV. These results demonstrate that targeted inductive biases can yield fast neural surrogates with substantially improved geometric fidelity.

item.title: One-point charge correlator as a probe for the odderon
item.dc:creator: Haotian Cao et al.
item.description:
Watchlist hit (energy correlator, infrared and collinear safe) — abstract only, not yet read for a briefing.

We propose the one-point charge correlator (OPCC) in transversely polarized deep inelastic scattering as a new probe of the spin-dependent odderon. The OPCC is an infrared and collinear safe observable constructed solely from the charge and angular information of final-state charged particles. Because the charge weight is odd under charge conjugation, the contribution of the C-even pomeron to the OPCC vanishes identically in the small-x eikonal limit, whereas the contribution of the C-odd spin-dependent odderon survives. We define a transverse single-spin asymmetry by normalizing the spin-dependent OPCC to the unpolarized charged-hadron one-point energy correlator. At small x, this asymmetry reduces to a ratio of spin-dependent odderon and pomeron contributions. We provide illustrative estimates of this asymmetry for Electron-Ion Collider kinematics within the small-x dipole framework with Balitsky–Kovchegov evolution to guide experimental studies. Dedicated measurements of the OPCC asymmetry with a transversely polarized proton beam would provide new quantitative constraints on the currently unconstrained spin-dependent odderon.

item.title: Computationally Efficient Description of Medium Response to Jets in Heavy Ion Collisions
item.dc:creator: Jorge Casalderrey-Solana et al.
item.description:
Only tangential to jet substructure per se: the paper computes the hydrodynamic wake (medium response) that contaminates the soft component of reconstructed jets in heavy-ion collisions, not substructure observables directly. Its relevance is that this soft contribution cannot be groomed away for most observables, so a correct wake description is a prerequisite for computing jet/substructure observables in AA. The concrete advance is an “Efficient Wake” procedure: precompute a library of 34 template (Green’s-function) solutions to (1+1)D linearized hydro on a Bjorken background for unit energy-momentum deposition (deposition times τ_temp^d = kΔτ, Δτ=0.4 fm/c, τ₀=0.4 to τ_f=13.6 fm/c, T_f=145 MeV ⇒ T₀=446 MeV), then reconstruct wakes in a radially expanding droplet by superposing templates with suitable rotations/boosts to fold in transverse radial flow at freezeout.

Benchmarked against full nonlinear (3+1)D MUSIC hydro for 50 representative partons at two energies, they find reasonable agreement and — the headline — a speedup of “at least tens of thousands” up to a factor 200,000, while giving a much better p_T spectrum (harder, matching data’s demand for more particles above ~2 GeV) than the constant+cosine Hybrid-Model treatment. Caveats stated: the approximations are not controlled by smallness of the perturbation (validity assessed only empirically via the 50-event comparison), and implementation in a jet Monte Carlo (where 10⁵–10⁶ wakes per analysis are needed) remains future work.

item.title: Hunting the Unseen: Deep Learning Analysis for Semi-Visible Jet Tagging
item.dc:creator: Miguel A. Avenda\~no-Bernal et al.
item.description:
Squarely a jet-substructure paper. It benchmarks five DL classifiers for SVJ (Z′→dark quarks, Hidden Valley) vs QCD dijet discrimination, combining global kinematics (MET, Δφ(MET,jet), M_jj, M_T) with substructure: primary Lund Jet Plane, two-point EEC e₂^(β=1), angularity τ_{α,1} for α=0.1,0.8,1.5, and charged-hadron multiplicity. Architectures: a ViT on 50×50 LJP images (patchified 10×10, 6 encoder blocks, 4 heads), JetLOV (RegNet learning node features on the C/A tree, feeding LundNet EdgeConv), an MLP on 15 high-level observables, and two fusion networks (ViT+MLP, JetLOV+MLP). Training on 300k+300k events across 18 BPs (m_Z′=2.5, 4.5 TeV; scans of m_ψd, r_inv, Λ_dark), with three held-out 3.5 TeV BPs to test interpolation across parameter space.

The key benchmark result for the field: global kinematic observables outperform both jet-representation networks individually; among substructure representations the hierarchical clustering-tree (JetLOV) beats LJP images; and fusing structured representations with global kinematics gives the best overall performance. This quantifies how much discrimination lives in radiation-pattern structure beyond MET/global variables — modest but complementary. Caveats visible in text: no pileup in the samples (angularity especially would need mitigation), Pythia default hadronisation parameters held fixed, and r_inv is not an explicit Pythia parameter but tuned via dark-hadron branching fractions. Full AUC numbers are in tables not reproduced in the provided text.

item.title: Soft functions for generalised angularity event shapes at NNLO
item.dc:creator: Emmet P. Byrne et al.
item.description:
Watchlist hit (event shape, event shapes) — abstract only, not yet read for a briefing.

We consider a class of dijet event shapes which tend to angularity in the forward limit. The factorisation formula for this class of event shapes differs from angularity only in the soft function. The NNLO soft function of an event shape in this class is therefore the only missing ingredient required for NNLL’ resummation. We describe a modular approach to the calculation of the soft function for any event shape in this class, at NLO and NNLO. Much of the structure of the soft function can be written in terms of a single rapidity integral. The remainder can be computed as a three-dimensional numerical integral for which we provide a code. To demonstrate the flexibility of our approach, we compute the NNLO soft function for three new families of event shapes in this class. Potential applications include the investigation of hadronisation effects at future e⁺ e⁻ colliders, or through the re-analysis of archived data.

item.title: Collinear fragmentation of pseudoscalar quarkonia from NLO NRQCD
item.dc:creator: Francesco Giovanni Celiberto et al.
item.description:
Watchlist hit (jet fragmentation) — abstract only, not yet read for a briefing.

We discuss a new family of publicly available collinear fragmentation functions (FFs) for pseudoscalar quarkonia, the NRFF1.0 set. It builds upon the Heavy-Flavor Non-Relativistic evolution (HF-NRevo) scheme, designed to describe heavy-hadron formation through leading-power fragmentation at moderate and large transverse momentum. Heavy-quarkonium production naturally involves both perturbative and non-perturbative QCD dynamics, from the production of the heavy QQ̅ pair to its formation into a physical bound state. Within NRFF1.0, Non-Relativistic Quantum Chromodynamics (NRQCD) provides the theoretical framework for calculating the FF inputs at the initial scale, which are subsequently evolved through the HF-NRevo scheme. This setup provides a precision baseline for investigating the underlying partonic hierarchy and jet structure across the moderate- to high-transverse-momentum regime. The explicit treatment of partonic channels and heavy-flavor thresholds makes this framework particularly suitable for exploring quarkonium-in-jet fragmentation, jet-quenching sensitivity, energy-loss mechanisms, and the emergence of medium-modified fragmentation patterns in the quark-gluon plasma.

item.title: "Transforming" LHCb: self-supervised maps of heavy-flavour decays
item.dc:creator: Marko Stamenkovic et al.
item.description:
Watchlist hit (flavour tagging, jet flavour) — abstract only, not yet read for a briefing.

Decays of beauty and charm hadrons provide sensitive probes of physics beyond the standard model, including decays with invisible particles, in which part of the final state leaves no reconstructed detector signature. The large heavy-flavour data samples recorded by the LHCb experiment at the CERN LHC, together with its precise tracking, displaced vertex reconstruction, and particle identification, make it particularly well suited to learning a map of reconstructed heavy-hadron decay environments directly from data. We propose to bring recent advances in jet flavour tagging at ATLAS and CMS to significantly improve on the performance of the current LHCb taggers and extend them to the reconstruction of heavy-flavour decays with several invisible particles in the final state. To achieve this, we introduce a self-supervised transformer architecture that learns the decay maps without flavour or exclusive-decay labels by inferring masked particle identification information and completing jets from which constituents have been removed. Across five classification tasks in simulated LHCb Open Data, the self-supervised model outperforms an otherwise identical transformer with random weights, and performs comparably to a fully supervised transformer. We achieve a tagging power of about 10\%. In addition, removing constituents from reconstructed exclusive decays also systematically increases the model anomaly score relative to random removals from the same heavy hadrons. We confirm this behaviour directly in 2017 LHCb proton-proton collision Open Data: the score increases for all eight studied heavy-flavour channels, and the signal region response exceeds that in the adjacent sidebands. These studies provide a proof of principle that mapping heavy-flavour decay environments through jets can transform flavour tagging in LHCb and extend the discovery reach for incomplete or otherwise unusual decays.

item.title: Likelihood-Based Unsupervised Anomaly Detection in CMS Dijet Events (Bhavishya Chebrolu
item.dc:creator: VIT-AP University et al.
item.description:
Trains a rational-quadratic neural spline flow (10 blocks, 256 hidden units, 8 bins) on 61 high-level dijet/event observables from CMS 2011B HT AOD open data (√s=7 TeV, 378,278 events, ~0.5 fb⁻¹), scoring events by −log p(x) with no signal model, MC, or sidebands. Selecting the 99.9th percentile (379 events) and running KS tests across all 61 features, the largest population-level deviations are overwhelmingly jet-substructure variables: leading-jet girth (D=0.575), τ₁/τ₂/τ₃ (0.548/0.541/0.518), the ECF ratio (0.508), τ₃₂ (0.498), τ₂₁ (0.441), width (0.386), then jet mass (0.373) and HT (0.343). The anomalous events show no m_jj resonance — a sliding-window bump hunt gives a look-elsewhere-corrected global p=6.0×10⁻⁴ (test stat 8.79), which they explicitly decline to call evidence.

For jet substructure the relevance is real but the framing is honest: substructure observables emerge as the dominant discriminants of the “non-QCD-like” tail, and the paper gives a useful discussion of why ECFs (recoil-free, subjet-free, IRC-safe) and N-subjettiness give coherent signals. Important self-stated caveats: the flow is trained and scored in-sample (no held-out split, acknowledged likelihood-scale bias); selecting the tail of a multivariate density trivially sculpts the marginals, so KS p-values (e.g. 10⁻¹¹⁹ for girth) are diagnostic only, not significances; and the τ₂₁/τ₃₂=0 spikes are known PF low-multiplicity artifacts. Methodological/exploratory contribution rather than a substructure measurement per se.

item.title: The Colors of Jet Quenching
item.dc:creator: Hannah Bossi et al.
item.description:
Watchlist hit (energy correlators) — abstract only, not yet read for a briefing.

We combine inclusive jet nuclear modification factors with energy-energy correlators to perform a data-driven extraction of the quark and gluon quenching factors and the medium resolution scale from the small-angle region. Taking coherent energy loss as a null hypothesis, we find jet quenching factors incompatible with Casimir scaling. Incorporating color decoherence through antenna energy loss improves the description of the data and restores Casimir scaling, providing evidence that the quark-gluon plasma partially resolves the internal structure of jets in heavy-ion collisions.

item.title: Energy-energy correlators and color decoherence from a generating functional
item.dc:creator: Yacine Mehtar-Tani
item.description:
Watchlist hit (energy correlators) — abstract only, not yet read for a briefing.
